Are neoclouds dead?

Let's look at $NBIS, $CRWV, $IREN and $APLD

Bull case vs. bear case. 🧵

$NBIS (Nebius)

One of the most diverse AI infra plays.

🐂 Bull case

🟢Q3 revenue: $981M, up 571% YoY.

🟢$12B in new contract value signed since Q3 began.

🟢AI Cloud adjusted EBITDA margin: 53%.

🟢Q3 customer prepayments covered over 100% of associated capex.

🐻 Bear case

🔴Data center delays pushed revenue into 2027.

🔴2027 capex guidance: $40–45B.

🔴Revenue guidance for 2026 was revised toward the lower end of its range.

My take: Exceptional demand and improving unit economics. Delays are the biggest risk.

$CRWV (CoreWeave)

The scale leader among these four.

🐂 Bull case

🟢Q3 revenue: $3.66B, up 168% YoY.

🟢Revenue backlog: $132.5B.

🟢FY2026 revenue guidance raised to $13–13.3B.

🟢Expanding relationships with major AI labs and enterprises.

🐻 Bear case

🔴Q3 net loss: $709M

🔴Quarterly net interest expense: $846M

🔴FY2026 capex guidance: $37–39B

🔴Heavy reliance on debt

My take: Massive growth, but financing costs and capital intensity deserve serious attention.

$IREN (IREN)

Combination of power ownership, data centers and AI compute.

🐂 Bull case

🟢Q1 FY27 AI Cloud revenue: $200M, up 182% QoQ.

🟢AI Cloud gross margin: 86%.

🟢Revenue backlog: $20.3B.

🟢More than $4B contracted ARR target for 2026 capacity.

🐻 Bear case

🔴The $4B+ ARR target has shifted from year-end to January–February 2027.

🔴FY2027 planned capex: $15B.

🔴Around $6B of that spending still requires additional financing or other funding sources.

My take: Right now, their asset value is close to their market cap. Market is pricing the business at almost $0

$APLD (Applied Digital)

A slightly different business model: building and leasing AI data centers to hyperscalers.

🐂 Bull case

🟢More than $41B in contracted base-term lease revenue.

🟢New 150 MW, 18-year hyperscaler lease worth $5.4B.

🟢Around 75% of contracted base-term revenue comes from investment-grade customers.

🟢Long-term leases provide substantial revenue visibility.

🐻 Bear case

🔴$6.4B debt versus $3.7B cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash at August 31.

🔴Q1 FY27 data center rental revenue was $79.1M; total revenue included significant fit-out services and hardware sales.

🔴New 150 MW lease delivery is not expected to begin until H1 2028.

My take: Strong contract book, but construction, financing and delivery are the real tests.

So, are neoclouds dead?

I think the opposite.

AI compute demand is real. The infrastructure buildout is real. And the contracts are getting bigger.

But not all neoclouds are created equal.

The next winners will be companies that can:

Secure power.

Deliver capacity on time.

Maintain attractive margins.

Finance expansion without destroying shareholder value.

The opportunity is massive. So are the risks.
